searchText: ok so maybe i am wandering into a minefield here 🙂 but why would eip-5806 new txn type be more technical debt than opcodes? https://twitter.com/0xfoobar/status/1769017748829385178 i think another nice thing about eip-5806 is that other "AA features" can be added piecemeal. like it doesn't preclude gas sponsorship from being added later There is far more code facilitating tx types than opcodes. Tests, txpool, and RPC especially how about calling a precompile (i think https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2803 is along these lines), or adding some bytes in the top 12 bytes of addresses to indicate the type of transaction? and also, in a "many transaction types" world, shouldn't adding txn types be easy? Precompiles today are pure functions and I think it should stay like that. Not sure what you mean about using the top 12 bytes, but we might eventually want to increase the address size so we shouldn't complicate that process further It isn't hard from a techincal perspecitve, but it is a lot more code. It's something to consider something hacky like `0xFF...<20 bytes address>` means "delegatecall this address" 🙂 In the transaction `to`? yea or provide 33 bytes, idk all the data types for `to` are 20 byte arrays, i think adding a new tx type would actually be far easier it really just comes down to the question: should ethereum be making bespoke solutions for every problem or should we create a general framework to let developers create solutions 5806 is a (good) bespoke solution. but 3074 is a framework i don't really understand the difference between a solution and a framework ethereum was built on the principle that instead of having bespoke apps for every use case (colored coins, name coins, dex, etc) it would have a vm for developers to create applications. extension of the protocol essentially. i don't see why we treat accounts differently. it's the whole point of AA! https://blog.ethereum.org/2015/07/05/on-abstraction well to me at least, allowing eoas to execute code seems like the more general solution, because it gives them the same status as contracts but it's not more general than 3074 and i wouldn't say it gives them the same status as contracts, because you can't even deploy code to eoa address this is the problem with a bespoke solution. we already know there are more things we want to do, such as tx sponsorship. we want account recovery. all possible with 3074, none with 5806. there are still things that we haven't even thought of yet, which will be possible 3074. 5806 doesn't provide that flexibility hmm. with 5806, these features can be added later though i am not convinced account abstraction is a "bespoke app" on the same level as colored coins or dexes really. it's something that should be in the protocol no? there will always be "the next thing" which the tx type should be able to do. the flavor of the month. things like this should not live at the prtocol level. we can't assume the protocol will be able to add new features forever 4337 is not in the protocol and seems like a good solution to account abstraction why not! upgrading the network comes with risk.. it isn't free to do. and proving things are useful beyond a doubt is already getting increasingly difficult. this will be especially true if ethereum continues to be successful. even something which seems unambiguously good like scaling data potentially benefits certain types of rollups more than others. if there are competing smart account standards, it can easily reach a stalemate where both/many factions want different modifications to the core protocol so their flavor is better. but possibly at the expensive of a competing approach the protocol should do the absolute minimal thing to unlock the next layer of developers. i'm surprised to see this as such a controversial statement i don't find the statement particularly controversial i think the controversy is around what constitutes "absolute minimal" 😀 5806 is not a complete solution to the problem set. if you bolt on what’s necessary to make 5806 comparable it will be much more complicated than 3074 i tried to design a tx type that did this a while ago. it ends up being rather complicated and inflexible https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2733

upgrading the network comes with risk.. it isn't free to do. and proving things are useful beyond a doubt is already getting increasingly difficult. this will be especially true if ethereum continues to be successful. even something which seems unambiguously good like scaling data potentially benefits certain types of rollups more than others.

if there are competing smart account standards, it can easily reach a stalemate where both/many factions want different modifications to the core protocol so their flavor is better. but possibly at the expensive of a competing approach
